- region "What ms-reader can see":
  - heading "What ms-reader can see" [level=3]
  - paragraph:
    - text: "SQL Server 16.0.4295.3, schemas sales: 1 table and 0 views. Discovered as"
    - code: formancy_reader
    - text: . Fingerprint
    - code: 94b2d94ccf2a
    - text: .
  - region "What this connection could not see":
    - heading "What this connection could not see" [level=4]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Each of these is
      - strong: cannot tell
      - text: ", not"
      - strong: does not exist
      - text: ": a table, key or relationship missing below may be there, out of this account’s sight."
    - list "What this connection could not see":
      - listitem:
        - code: The whole scope
        - text: referenced-by this account lacks VIEW DEFINITION on the database, which is what lists every foreign key on a table in any schema, so a key on a table it cannot see may refer to any table in scope
      - listitem:
        - code: The whole scope
        - text: row-security this account lacks VIEW DEFINITION on the database, which is what lists every security policy, so a security policy it cannot see may filter any table or view in scope
      - listitem:
        - code: Schema sales
        - text: objects without VIEW DEFINITION on schema sales, the catalog lists only the tables and views this account holds a permission on, so one it cannot see is absent without trace
      - listitem:
        - code: sales.order
        - text: "checks ck_order_status: the expression is hidden without VIEW DEFINITION"
      - listitem:
        - code: sales.order
        - text: "defaults status: the definition of its default df_order_status is hidden without VIEW DEFINITION"
      - listitem:
        - code: sales.order
        - text: "foreign-keys fk_order_approved_by references a table this account cannot see: the key and its own columns are visible, the name of its target and of the target's columns are not"
      - listitem:
        - code: sales.order
        - text: "foreign-keys fk_order_created_by references a table this account cannot see: the key and its own columns are visible, the name of its target and of the target's columns are not"
      - listitem:
        - code: sales.order
        - text: "foreign-keys fk_order_customer references a table this account cannot see: the key and its own columns are visible, the name of its target and of the target's columns are not"
  - heading "Tables and views" [level=4]
  - list "Tables and views":

        - code: sales.order
        - text: table

text.Publish:
- main "Publish":
  - heading "Publish" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: "One bundle: the form as the presentation step left it, its bindings to sales.order on"
    - code: pg
    - text: ", the policy, and the snapshot they were generated from. The server checks all of it again before it writes anything, and keeps every version it has published."
  - paragraph: Version 2 of pg-order is published now, and it is somebody else's. Publishing waits until you rebase on it.
  - paragraph:
    - button "Publish" [disabled]
  - alert:
    - paragraph: Somebody published version 2 while you worked. Yours was not published, and theirs is untouched.

text.Drift:
- main "Drift":
  - heading "Drift" [level=2]
  - paragraph: "Compare a published form with its database as it is now. Only what the form rests on is compared: its table and its lookups’ targets. Something this connection can no longer see is an access change, never a deletion."
  - text: Form id
  - textbox "Form id": pg-order
  - button "Check drift"
  - region "Version 3 of pg-order, against the database now":
    - heading "Version 3 of pg-order, against the database now" [level=3]
    - status: 3 changes, 1 blocking.
    - heading "What the published form may still do" [level=4]
    - list "What the published form may still do":
      - listitem: "Read: blocked by the changes below"
      - listitem: "Create: blocked by the changes below"
      - listitem: "Update: blocked by the changes below"
      - listitem: "As a whole: not to be used as published until the blocking changes are reviewed."
    - heading "Blocking" [level=4]
    - paragraph: "Blocks the form as published: a write it offers is stopped, or a field it shows can no longer be read, until it is reviewed."
    - list "Blocking":
      - listitem:
        - paragraph:
          - text: blocking
          - code: column-dropped
          - text: on sales.order, column notes
        - paragraph: notes is gone, and the form binds it to notes. The form is blocked until it is reviewed.
        - paragraph: Affects Remarks (notes).
    - heading "Review" [level=4]
    - paragraph: Blocks nothing. A person has something to decide.
    - list "Review":
      - listitem:
        - paragraph:
          - text: review
          - code: column-added
          - text: on sales.order, column memo
        - paragraph: memo is new (text, nullable). It can be added to the form; the published form is unchanged.
        - paragraph: Affects no field of this form.
      - listitem:
        - paragraph:
          - text: review
          - code: possible-rename
          - text: on sales.order, column notes
        - paragraph: "notes is gone and memo is new with the same definition (text). If it is notes renamed, confirm it: nothing is inferred, and until then they are reported as a dropped column and a new one."
        - paragraph: Affects Remarks (notes).
  - paragraph:
    - button "Regenerate, keeping your presentation"
  - region "Versions of pg-order":
    - heading "Versions of pg-order" [level=3]
    - region "Download a version":
      - heading "Download a version" [level=4]
      - paragraph: "The file the server stored, byte for byte: another deployment imports it, and git compares it."
      - text: Version to download
      - combobox "Version to download":
        - option "Version 1"
        - option "Version 2"
        - option "Version 3" [selected]
      - link "Download version 3":
        - /url: blob:http://studio.invalid/<uuid>
    - region "Restore a version":
      - heading "Restore a version" [level=4]
      - paragraph: Restoring publishes an older version again as version 4, with the policy it had, when the database can still serve it. It changes no table.
      - text: Version to restore
      - combobox "Version to restore":
        - option "Version 1" [selected]
        - option "Version 2"
      - button "Restore version 1"
      - paragraph: "Version 1: “Order”, 9 fields, bound to sales.order on pg."
    - alert:
      - paragraph: "Version 1 cannot be restored: the database has changed in a way it cannot serve."
      - heading "What blocks it" [level=5]
      - list "What blocks it":
        - listitem:
          - paragraph:
            - text: blocking
            - code: column-dropped
            - text: on sales.order, column notes
          - paragraph: notes is gone, and the form binds it to notes. The form is blocked until it is reviewed.
          - paragraph: Affects Remarks (notes).
  - region "Import a version":
    - heading "Import a version" [level=3]
    - paragraph: A version file is one version as a studio downloads it, from this deployment or another. It keeps its form id and its connection’s name, which this deployment’s allowlist resolves to its own database. The server checks it as it checks a publish, and against this database as it checks a restore.
    - text: Version file
    - button "Version file"
